'''Paul Leo Butzer''' (15 April 1928 – 9 September 2026) was a German mathematician who specialised in [[Mathematical analysis|analysis]] ([[approximation theory]], [[harmonic analysis]]). He was born in Germany but studied in Montreal and Toronto, Canada. He returned to Germany for his [[habilitation]] and then taught at the [[RWTH Aachen University]] from 1958. Besides mathematics, he was interested in its history and studied the life and work of mathematicians, beginning in the Carolingian era, publishing a biography of [[Elwin Bruno Christoffel]]. Some of his scientific works were translated.

== Life and work ==
Butzer was born in [[Mülheim]] on 15 April 1928,<ref name="Maths History-1928">{{cite web |last1=O'Connor | first1=John J. |last2=Robertson | first2=Edmund F. |author2-link=E. F. Robertson | title=Paul Butzer | website=Maths History | date=15 April 1928 | url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Butzer/ | access-date=12 September 2026}}</ref> the son of an engineer and a mother who studied mathematics at [[RWTH Aachen University]] who had met as students.<ref name="Maths History-1928" /> Paul grew up with a younger brother, [[Karl W. Butzer|Karl]], who also became a scientist.<ref name="Maths History-1928" /><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Butzer | first1=Paul L. | last2=Stens | first2=Rudolf L. | title=A retrospective on research visits of Paul Butzer's Aachen research group to Eastern Europe and Tenerife | journal=Sampling Theory, Signal Processing, and Data Analysis | volume=20 | issue=2 | date=2022 | article-number=17 | issn=2730-5716 | doi=10.1007/s43670-022-00034-6 | bibcode=2022STSPD..20...17B | url=https://link.springer.com/10.1007/s43670-022-00034-6 | access-date=12 September 2026}}</ref> As opponents of the Nazis, Butzer's parents left Germany with their children in 1937 and moved to England. During [[World War II]], they relocated to Canada, where Butzer attended school in [[Montreal]] and studied mathematics at Loyola College (later [[Concordia University]]), completing his bachelor's degree in 1948.<ref name="Maths History-1928" /> He then pursued further studies at the [[University of Toronto]], including studying under [[Harold Scott MacDonald Coxeter]] and [[William Tutte]], and obtained his Ph.D. in 1951 under the supervision of [[George G. Lorentz]] (on [[Bernstein polynomials]]).<ref name="Maths History-1928" /><ref name="Butzer">{{cite journal | last=Butzer | first=Paul L. | title=A retrospective on 60 years of approximation theory and associated fields | journal=Journal of Approximation Theory | volume=160 | issue=1–2 | date=2009 | doi=10.1016/j.jat.2009.05.004 | pages=3–18 | url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0021904509001038 | access-date=12 September 2026}}</ref> In 1952, he became a lecturer and then an assistant professor at [[McGill University]]. In 1955-56, he lived in Paris and then in [[Mainz]]. He decided to stay in Germany, where he completed his habilitation at the [[University of Freiburg]], taught [[University of Würzburg|in Würzburg]], and starting in 1958, at RWTH Aachen University. In 1962, he was appointed professor there. In 1963, he began organizing international conferences on [[approximation theory]] at the [[Oberwolfach Research Institute for Mathematics]], later together with [[Béla Szőkefalvi-Nagy]].<ref name="Maths History-1928" /><ref name="Butzer" />

In addition to approximation theory and its connections to [[Fourier analysis]] and semigroups of operators in [[Banach space|Banach spaces]], Butzer also worked on probability theory ([[central limit theorem]] and related [[convergence tests]] issues), [[sampling Theory|sampling theory]], and [[signal analysis]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.matha.rwth-aachen.de/de/mitarbeiter/butzer/|title=Lehrstuhl A für Mathematik, RWTH Aachen – Mitarbeiter|website=www.matha.rwth-aachen.de}}</ref>

He also delved into the history of mathematics, particularly in its connection with [[Aachen]]. He studied figures such as [[Peter Gustav Lejeune Dirichlet]], [[Eduard Helly]], [[Eugène Catalan]], [[Pafnuty Chebyshev]], [[Charles Jean de la Vallée Poussin]], the history of [[Spline (mathematics)|splines]], [[Otto Blumenthal]], mathematics in the [[Carolingian-era|Carolingian era]], and [[Elwin Bruno Christoffel]], on whom he published a book.<ref name="Maths History-1928" />

Butzer was a member of the Royal Society of Sciences in Liège and the [[Royal Belgian Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="y741">{{cite web | title=Paul Butzer | website=academieroyale.be | url=https://academieroyale.be/fr/who-who-detail/relations/paul-butzer/ | language=fr | access-date=12 September 2026}}</ref> He was an honorary member of the [[Hamburg Mathematical Society|Mathematical Society in Hamburg]].<ref name="v585">{{cite web | title=Ehrenmitglieder der Mathematischen Gesellschaft | work=Mathematische Gesellschaft in Hamburg (gegr. 1690) | url=https://www.mathges.hamburg/Ehrenmitglieder.html | language=de | access-date=12 September 2026}}</ref> He received honorary doctorates from three universities: [[University of Liège|Liège]], [[University of York|York]], and [[West University of Timișoara|Timișoara]].<ref name="Maths History-1928"/>

Butzer died on 9 September 2026, at the age of 98.<ref name="Trauer">{{cite web | title=Traueranzeigen von Paul L. Butzer | website=Aachen gedenkt | url=https://www.aachen-gedenkt.de/traueranzeige/paul-l-butzer | language=de | access-date=12 September 2026}}</ref>
